inputs.userGoal: リソースグループをSREagent-labとして再構築し、Azure SRE Agent PaaSを含めて再デプロイする
subGoals: Cost-optimized production: Japan East single-region, small workload, scale-to-zero where supported
Security baseline: managed identity, Key Vault, TLS, and private PostgreSQL connectivity
Persistent commerce data: PostgreSQL-backed inventory, orders, order items, and delivery addresses

deploymentInputs.deploymentPrincipalId: Required object ID for the user or service principal running deployment; validated before RBAC deployment
deploymentInputs.postgresAdministratorPassword: Required secure value generated or supplied at deployment time and never committed
deploymentInputs.imageTag: Required immutable build ID or version; latest is not used for application revisions
deploymentInputs.resourceToken: Required globally stable lowercase alphanumeric workload token

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides an isolated lifecycle and cost boundary for the production workload.
alternativesConsidered: Reuse an existing shared resource group
reasoning.tradeoffs: A dedicated group adds one management boundary but prevents accidental coupling to unrelated workloads.

resources.name: azvnt{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides private routing between Container Apps and PostgreSQL.
alternativesConsidered: Public PostgreSQL endpoint with firewall rule
reasoning.tradeoffs: VNet integration adds deployment complexity but removes public database exposure.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The VNet is deployed into the production resource group.

resources.name: azca{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: A dedicated /27 delegated subnet satisfies the Workload Profiles Container Apps Environment requirement.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Workload Profiles networking preserves address space while retaining Consumption workload profile support.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The subnet is a child of the application VNet.

resources.name: azdb{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: PostgreSQL private access requires a dedicated delegated subnet.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Delegated networking is simple and secure for this single-VNet deployment but ties the server to the VNet.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The subnet is a child of the application VNet.

resources.name: aznsg{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Limits database subnet ingress to PostgreSQL traffic originating from the Container Apps infrastructure subnet.
alternativesConsidered: Rely only on subnet delegation and PostgreSQL access controls
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds network policy maintenance but provides defense in depth.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NSG is created before association with the delegated database subnet.

resources.name: {postgresServerName}.postgres.database.azure.com
resources.subtype: PostgreSQL private DNS zone and VNet link

reasoning.whyChosen: Required for name resolution of a VNet-integrated PostgreSQL Flexible Server.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The service-required DNS name is an intentional exception to the generic az{prefix}{token} naming convention.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The zone is linked to the VNet before PostgreSQL is provisioned.

resources.name: azlog{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Centralizes Container Apps, database, Key Vault, and application telemetry with a cost cap.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A 30-day retention and 1 GB daily cap control cost but limit long-term incident analysis.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The workspace is deployed into the production resource group before dependent services.

resources.name: azai{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides application-level request, dependency, exception, and performance telemetry.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Telemetry adds ingestion cost, controlled by the shared workspace quota.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Workspace-based Application Insights requires the Log Analytics workspace.

resources.name: azmon{resourceToken}
resources.subtype: Azure Monitor Workspace for Azure SRE Agent

reasoning.whyChosen: Azure SRE Agent requires an Azure Monitor Workspace for the issues it produces.
alternativesConsidered: Create the agent manually outside IaC
reasoning.tradeoffs: The workspace is deployed in Australia East because Azure SRE Agent is not available in Japan East.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The workspace is deployed in the workload resource group before the SRE Agent.

resources.name: azsre{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides the requested Azure SRE Agent PaaS for evidence-based investigation of the Store, API, PostgreSQL, and monitoring resources.
alternativesConsidered: Custom agent hosted on Container Apps
reasoning.tradeoffs: The agent incurs always-on AAU charges while it exists. Manual mode and read-only roles require human approval before changes.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The agent stores issues in Azure Monitor Workspace and reads workload telemetry through resource-group-scoped RBAC.

references.title: Azure SRE Agent pricing and billing

resources.name: azid{pullToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a stable identity for ACR pull without embedded registry credentials.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The identity is shared because both apps require the same single AcrPull permission and no other role.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The identity is created before role assignments and Container Apps.

resources.name: azid{apiToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates API secret access from the shared image-pull identity to reduce blast radius.
alternativesConsidered: One shared identity for every role
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds one identity and role assignment but enforces least privilege.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The identity is created before Key Vault role assignment and API deployment.

resources.name: azcr{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Basic ACR is sufficient for three low-volume images and supports managed identity pull.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public ACR endpoint is retained to avoid Premium fixed cost; authentication remains private through managed identity and admin credentials are disabled.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The registry must exist before AcrPull assignment and application image publication.

resources.name: guid(acr, identity, AcrPull)

reasoning.whyChosen: Allows the user-assigned identity to pull private application images from ACR.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Role assignment names must be GUIDs and therefore intentionally cannot use the az{prefix}{token} convention.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Both the registry scope and identity principal must exist before assignment.

references.title: Container Apps managed identity image pull

resources.name: azkv{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Stores generated PostgreSQL credentials and supports Container Apps secret references through managed identity.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public network access is enabled for initial reliable secret reference deployment, while Azure RBAC prevents anonymous access. Private endpoint hardening is deferred to avoid bootstrapping and cost complexity.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The vault must exist before secret role assignments and database secret creation.

resources.name: guid(vault, identity, secretsUser)
resources.subtype: Key Vault Secrets User role assignment

reasoning.whyChosen: Allows Container Apps to resolve Key Vault-backed secrets at runtime without write permission.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Role assignment names must be GUIDs; runtime access is read-only.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The vault and application identity must exist before least-privilege assignment.

resources.name: guid(vault, deployer, secretsOfficer)
resources.subtype: Key Vault Secrets Officer deployment role

reasoning.whyChosen: Allows the deployment identity to create and rotate generated database secrets while avoiding vault-wide administration.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The deployment principal ID must be supplied explicitly and retains secret-management capability until the role is removed.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The Key Vault scope must exist before role assignment.

references.title: Azure built-in roles for Key Vault

resources.name: azpg{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides persistent relational storage for products, stock, orders, order items, and delivery addresses at the lowest practical production cost.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Burstable single-zone compute is not highly available and can experience CPU credit limits. Seven-day local backup provides basic recovery but no cross-region disaster recovery.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Private subnet and DNS must exist, and generated administrator credentials must be stored in Key Vault before server provisioning.

resources.name: azcae{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Hosts all three independently scalable apps with VNet access to private PostgreSQL and centralized logs.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Single-zone environment and scale-to-zero reduce cost but permit cold starts and do not meet strict high-availability targets.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The dedicated subnet and Log Analytics workspace must exist before environment creation.

resources.name: azsto{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Publishes the buyer-facing Vue storefront independently from operational controls.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Scale-to-zero creates possible cold starts. Container hosting preserves the existing Docker deployment model.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Environment, registry, identity, and pull permission are required before app creation.

resources.name: azapi{resourceToken}

reasoning.whyChosen: Hosts the product and order APIs with private database connectivity and centralized telemetry.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A public API endpoint is required by the browser-based storefront. CORS is restricted, but authentication and rate limiting remain application responsibilities.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The API requires compute, image pull, Key Vault access, database availability, and telemetry configuration.

overallReasoning.summary: Deploy the SREagent-lab resource group with the production workload in Japan East and Azure SRE Agent plus its Azure Monitor Workspace in Australia East. The workload uses VNet-integrated Container Apps, managed ACR access, private PostgreSQL, centralized secrets, and centralized monitoring.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Cost priority intentionally overrides full production WAF defaults: Container Apps can scale to zero instead of maintaining two replicas; PostgreSQL uses Burstable single-zone compute instead of zone-redundant HA; ACR remains Basic with public network access instead of Premium private endpoint. Store and API remain public because they serve buyers. PostgreSQL is private and reachable only through the integrated VNet. Azure-managed encryption at rest is used; customer-managed keys are deferred. Azure platform DDoS protection is used without a paid DDoS Protection plan. WAF and API gateway rate limiting are deferred; application request validation remains mandatory. All resources inherit environment, application, managedBy, and costCenter tags from the deployment. No tenant insights were available from the environment-insights tool.

operations.deploymentSequence: Phase 1 deploys shared infrastructure, PostgreSQL, bootstrap Store and API apps, and captures their FQDNs. Phase 2 builds immutable application images, updates both apps, and runs smoke tests.
operations.secretRotation: Generate a new PostgreSQL password, update the server credential and Key Vault postgres-admin-password secret, then restart or create a new API revision and verify database connectivity before retiring the previous secret version.
operations.secretRecovery: List deleted Key Vault secrets, recover postgres-admin-username or postgres-admin-password within the 90-day retention window, then create a new API revision. If recovery is not appropriate, regenerate the database credential and execute the rotation procedure.
operations.databaseAdministration: Routine schema changes run through versioned Flyway migrations from the API deployment. Azure control-plane operations handle backup restore and server maintenance. No always-on bastion or administration VM is deployed; exceptional SQL access uses a time-limited operator-approved Container Apps job on the integrated environment and is removed after use.
operations.highAvailabilityTrigger: Revisit zone-redundant PostgreSQL, minimum replicas of two, longer backup retention, and geo-recovery when an availability SLO is introduced, daily order volume becomes business critical, or measured recovery objectives exceed the accepted outage window.
operations.recoveryObjectives: For this non-critical small production workload, target manual recovery within four hours and at most one hour of data loss. Automated regional failover is out of scope. Restore procedures and Azure Monitor alerts must be tested before treating the service as business critical.
operations.monitoringScope: API request and dependency telemetry uses Application Insights. Store uses Container Apps platform metrics, availability checks, and stdout/stderr logs in Log Analytics. Azure SRE Agent receives read-only Monitoring Reader and Log Analytics Reader access at SREagent-lab scope and runs investigations in Manual mode.
operations.networkEvolution: The delegated PostgreSQL subnet is a deliberate low-cost constraint. Reassess private endpoints and hub-spoke connectivity before adding cross-region or cross-VNet consumers.
operations.logRetention: Thirty-day retention is accepted for this small production demo; extend it when audit or compliance requirements exceed 30 days.

plan.validation: Japan East availability and quota were checked for Container Apps and PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Australia East availability was checked for Microsoft.Monitor/accounts and Microsoft.Monitor/observabilityAgents. All dependency names, subnet delegations, identity assignments, preview API constraints, and SKU constraints must pass Bicep compilation and Azure what-if before deployment.
